test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If ‘u’ is the object-distance, ‘v’ is the image-distance and ‘f’ is the focal length of a spherical mirror then which of the following is a correct expression for the mirror formula?
solution:
The correct answer is **__1/v + 1/u = 1/f.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

Spherical Mirror:

__
 
• A spherical mirror is part of a hollow sphere, whose one side is reflecting and the other side is opaque.
 
• Two types of spherical mirrors are:

 
• Concave mirror, whose reflecting surface is towards the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.
 
• Convex mirror, whose reflecting surface is away from the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part.

EXPLANATION__:

 
• Mirror Formula: The following formula is known as the mirror formula, which represents the relation between focal length, image distance, and object distance

Rightarrow (1)/(f)=(1)/(u)+(1)/(v) 

Where, f = focal length, v = the distance of the image from the mirror, and u = the distance of the object from the mirror.
